# DockTabOverflowNL's reorder test releases its drag before the drag arms

> **Correction (2026-10-21, before the PR):** this body first blamed the lazily imported tab SortZone. An experiment refuted that. Holding `SortZone.mjs` for 4 s delays the tabs' first render too, and when the seven tabs appear, all of them already carry `neo-draggable`. The measured mechanism is below.

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockTabOverflowNL.spec.mjs:108` ("a reordered group still shows the control once its tabs overflow, and the menu reaches them") fails intermittently in the E2E (Brain-gated tier) job. I added the test in #19895 (for #19885).

- **Verified:** on the dev push `bb9c8742a3` (run 39582656813, job 119163845858), both tries failed at `:128`. After the drag, the first two tabs still read `['Strategy', 'Swarm']` when the 5 s poll expires. Each try took about 7 s, page load included.
- **Reported by @neo-opus-grace, not re-read:** the dev push `31738b0b35` (run 39574266240), and #19784's head `2e1dc1cdbd` on attempt 1. That PR's retry failed one line earlier, on a null `boundingBox` at `:123`.

## The Problem

The test waits for seven tab buttons. It then presses Strategy and travels to Swarm in one gesture of about 550 ms: `mouse.down`, 30 move steps, `mouse.up`. A tab drag only exists once the App Worker has armed it, and shortly after first paint the dock can still rebuild its tab header buttons. A gesture that travels and releases inside that window never arms, so the order never changes and `:128` times out. A box read inside it can come back null, which is the `:123` symptom.

Measured locally (headless Chromium, 2026-10-21). For each run I logged when the seven tabs appeared, whether the drag armed (`neo-is-dragging` on the toolbar, `.neo-dragproxy` in the DOM), and header-button removals around the gesture:

- **Passing runs** arm 114–178 ms after `mousedown`. Header churn follows only the release, from the drop's own projection.
- **Failing runs** never arm, even 600 ms after release. One shows ten header buttons removed 2 ms before the press.
- **Clustering:** the failures cluster on the fastest boots, with the seven tabs present roughly 210–500 ms after `goto`.
- **Totals:** across four unthrottled batches, the original gesture failed 8 of 39 runs. With 4× CPU throttling the boot is slow, and 6 of 6 passed.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The arming chain is asynchronous by construction:**
  1. The mouse sensor starts a drag only past `delay: 100` and `minDistance: 5` (`src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs`).
  2. `Neo.main.addon.DragDrop#onDragStart` forwards `drag:start` to the App Worker.
  3. `SortZone#onDragStart` awaits `owner.getDomRect`.
  4. `DragZone#dragStart` awaits `Neo.main.addon.DragDrop.setConfigs`, and only then adds `neo-is-dragging` to the owner toolbar.
- **Design authority:** `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs` — "Delay in ms before a drag OP starts." The start is asynchronous by design, so the gesture has to wait until it is armed. The fix belongs in the spec.
- **The boot-time rebuild:** the dock rebuilding its tab header buttons shortly after first paint is observed, but its cause is not identified (see Out of Scope).

## The Fix

Add `dragTabOnto(page, toolbar, source, target)` to the spec. It waits for the source to be visible, presses, and moves 8 px (past `minDistance`). It then waits, web-first, for `neo-is-dragging` on the toolbar, reads the target's box, travels in 30 steps, and releases. It uses no fixed sleep.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The spec's reorder gesture travels only after the toolbar carries `neo-is-dragging`, with no fixed sleep.
- [ ] AC-2: The PR carries a receipt taken under the same conditions: the original gesture fails some runs, and the fixed one passes every run, fast boots included.
- [ ] AC-3: The spec passes the PR's E2E (Brain-gated tier) run.

## Out of Scope

- The boot-time rebuild of the dock's tab header buttons. It is observed (ten buttons removed at the press in one failing run), its cause is not identified, and it is captured as a defect-note rather than fixed here.
- `DockDragDropNL.spec.mjs`'s fixed 2.5 s settle. It is green.
- The `IssuesShowcase.spec.mjs` `#19928` arm's flake, which has a different cause.
